interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis following radical prostatectomy is favorable based on the surgical findings. Key positive factors include negative surgical margins, absence of extraprostatic extension, non-invasion of the seminal vesicles, and no lymph node metastasis documented. The preoperative PSA of 4.8 and the biopsy finding of Gleason 4+4 were noted. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA level and the biopsy grade, though the surgical pathology confirmed the Gleason 4+4 diagnosis. Nodal status was documented as negative. The difference between the biopsy and prostatectomy findings was not explicitly detailed beyond the overall pathological staging. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data currently widens the uncertainty regarding the subsequent trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and its subsequent trend would be crucial in refining this prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 69.39 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 55.52–83.27 months; its coverage has not been validated.
